children: The LiveView Studio pane that ships nodes, edges, and a pinned root to the Graph Renderer — Barkpark's answer to Obsidian's graph.

Graph View is a LiveComponent named GraphView, mounted in LiveView Studio and bound to the client via the GraphPane phx-hook. The server runs a Graph Traversal from a chosen Document, then renders a container carrying three data attributes the hook reads on connect:
data-edges — the edges between them, sourced from the Content Edges Table
data-root — the id of the traversal root
data-root is not decoration. The Graph Renderer

and the Force Simulation lays everything else out around it. Drop the root and the layout has no anchor — the graph drifts and the "you are here" reading is lost. Traversal therefore always emits its root explicitly so the pane can forward it.

The LiveComponent does the data work (traversal, Blast Radius context, Orphan Node and Phantom Node computation) and hands a static payload across the wire; the Graph Renderer (bp-graph.js) does all drawing and physics. This keeps LiveView out of the per-frame loop — the same discipline that keeps Postgres Search off the request hot path. The same edges are also reachable headlessly: /v1/graph on the HTTP API v1 serves them to non-Studio clients.
This pane is the Barkpark side of the Graph Comparison against Obsidian's graph — the reason this very vault exists.
